samples.summary: New `mergeInlineStyle` key-deletion behavior is only pinned for boolean toggles; the CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE / `href: undefined` clears it also changed go through assertions that pass under both old and new behavior
samples.evidence: `mergeInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:316) now deletes any key whose patch value is `undefined`, which changes the stored shape for every clear — CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE (color/fontSize/bold/...), `removeLink`'s `{ href: undefined }`, and the superscript/subscript mutual-exclusion write at block-helpers.ts:339-343. The only tests that touch those paths are document.test.ts:161-211, which assert `expect(after.bold).toBeFalsy()` / `expect(bRun?.style.bold).toBeFalsy()` — true whether the key is absent or present-with-`undefined`, i.e. green before and after the change. The comment at document.test.ts:180-184 still documents the pre-change spread ('writes `undefined` to every cleared key … Asserting falsy keeps the test tolerant of either representation'), so nothing pins that CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE now removes the keys or that a fully-cleared run re-merges with an unstyled neighbour. Searched: grep CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, `href: undefined`, `'href' in`, mergeInlineStyle across packages/docs/test and packages/frontend/tests; no block-helpers unit test file for it.

samples.summary: The lazy-cascade motivation (cleared flag lets a later style redefinition apply) is asserted nowhere
samples.evidence: The `styleOffAsClear` doc comment and the test comments (document.test.ts:303-306) justify the change partly by 'the dead flag also pinned it against a later style redefinition'. No test toggles a boolean off and then redefines the block's named style to verify the run now picks the flag up. packages/docs/test/store/named-styles.test.ts has `updateStyleDefinition` tests but only for block spacing/registry, never combined with a toggled-off inline run. The tests in the diff only assert the stored key is absent, which is the mechanism, not the claimed consequence.

samples.summary: `styleOffAsClear` branches not covered: per-document style overrides, mixed-block ranges, and the missing-block fallback
samples.evidence: `styleOffAsClear` resolves defaults from `resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), this._document.styles)`, but the only exception test (document.test.ts:345) uses the *built-in* heading-6 italic. Nothing exercises (a) a doc-level override in `_document.styles` supplying the flag, (b) a cross-block range where one slice is a paragraph (clear) and another a heading-6 (keep explicit false) — the decision is per-slice, so this is a distinct behavior, or (c) the `block === undefined` fallback (`defaults = {}`) at document.ts:409-411. Also nothing pins the deliberate `pageNumber` exclusion documented at document.ts:34-37.

samples.summary: Collapsed-caret (pending style) toggle-off is not covered by any #749 test even though it flows through the new clearing path
samples.evidence: `toggleStyle` stores the computed `resolved` (containing `bold: false`) into `pending` at text-editor.ts:2899, and `createPendingStyle.consumeForInsert` (packages/docs/src/view/pending-style.ts:34) later replays it through `doc.applyInlineStyle`, so `styleOffAsClear` applies there too. No test in packages/docs/test/view/pending-style.test.ts or pending-style-integration.test.ts asserts that typing after a collapsed toggle-off yields a run with the key absent (they only assert `pending.has()` and style presence). The yorkie-doc-store comment added by this diff claims 'every B/I/U/S toggle-off' emits the clear, so the collapsed half of that claim is unverified.

samples.summary: `'bold' in (cd?.style ?? {})` degrades to a vacuous assertion if the run is not found
samples.evidence: `expect('bold' in (cd?.style ?? {})).toBe(false)` passes trivially when `cd` is `undefined` (the `?? {}` fallback has no keys). The preceding line 362 would fail first today, so the test is not currently vacuous, but the fallback hides run-lookup regressions; asserting `cd` is defined (or using a non-optional lookup) would keep both assertions load-bearing.
